labels.label: rem:definition_semi_locally_simply_connected

hypotheses.note: only local connectedness used
homotopy reading GX.AlmostTrivial (WP-26e SCOPE (a)), unruled; at least as strong as the literal notion

findings: RamcovGX.tex:1455-1457: 'X is semi-locally simply connected iff it is semi-locally simply connected in itself' holds only in the direction slsc ⇒ slsc in itself (GX.isSLSCIn_univ_of_semilocallySimplyConnected). The converse is false: the harmonic archipelago (a Peano continuum in ℝ³, locally contractible off its base point) has every loop at the base point homotopic to loops in arbitrarily small neighbourhoods, so it is slsc in itself in the sense of def:semi_locally_simple_connectedness, but π₁ ≠ 1 and it is not semi-locally simply connected. 'Almost trivial' differs from 'trivial' exactly for spaces which are not homotopically Hausdorff. The counterexample is not formalized.

labels.label: rem:simple_cases

hypotheses.note: the linear model holds for every closed proper linear subspace of a real normed space, codimension 1 included

read as LOCALLY FLAT (GX.isSLSCIn_of_locally_linear): every x ∈ X (in U or not) has an open V ∋ x and V ≃ₜ E with EITHER V ⊆ U (an ordinary chart inside U, so points of U far from X∖U and the case X∖U = ∅ are covered) OR V∖U = φ⁻¹(L) for a closed proper linear subspace L. Round 1 required the flat alternative at every point, which no chart at a point of U far from X∖U satisfies (0 ∈ L); fixed in round 2.

hypotheses.paper: a basis of neighbourhoods V with V ∩ U slsc in V
hypotheses.note: one neighbourhood per point suffices, but it is required OPEN (the paper's basis need not consist of open sets); openness is used to transport IsSLSCAt along the open embedding V ↪ X
homotopy reading GX.AlmostTrivial (WP-26e SCOPE (a)), unruled; at least as strong as the literal notion

hypotheses.paper: X a simplicial complex, X∖U a union of facets, U dense and locally connected
hypotheses.note: local connectedness of U and any dimension condition not used; 'facets' read as (closed) faces; U dense kept

GX.isSLSCIn_compl_faces_of_locallyFinite: X = |K| for a LOCALLY FINITE geometric simplicial complex of a real normed space (closed faces a locally finite family of E; mathlib Geometry.SimplicialComplex, subspace topology); GX.isSLSCIn_compl_faces is the finite case. Local finiteness is used only to make the union of faces not containing the base point closed. Complexes that are not locally finite / the weak topology are not stated.

findings: RamcovGX.tex:1462: the codimension ≥ 2 condition is not needed for semi-local simple connectedness in X: for any closed proper linear subspace L of ℝⁿ (codimension 1 included) ℝⁿ ∖ L is slsc in ℝⁿ by radial contraction (GX.isSLSCIn_compl_submodule); the codimension condition only matters for U being connected / X∖U skeletal.
RamcovGX.tex:1465: 'then U is locally simply connected at every point of X' is read as 'semi-locally simply connected at every point of X' (the notion just defined).

RamcovGX.tex:1462: the simplicial case needs no dimension condition either: for a finite simplicial complex K and S a union of closed faces with |K|∖S dense, |K|∖S is slsc in |K| by radial contraction inside the closed star of the base point (GX.isSLSCIn_compl_faces, via GX.isSLSCAt_of_radial_contraction).
questions: 'X∖U is a codimension at least 2 submanifold' is read as LOCALLY FLAT: every point of X has an open chart V ≃ₜ E which is either contained in U or carries V∖U onto a closed proper linear subspace (GX.isSLSCIn_of_locally_linear). Topological codimension-≥2 submanifolds which are not locally flat (wild arcs in ℝ³, e.g. Fox–Artin) are NOT stated in Lean: whether the claim holds for them is not known to us (radial contraction is unavailable at a wild point), so stating it with a sorry would risk a false theorem. Is local flatness intended?

'X is a simplicial complex and X∖U is a union of facets' is read as: X = |K| for a LOCALLY FINITE geometric simplicial complex K (subspace topology of a real normed space), X∖U a union of closed FACES of K (not facets = maximal faces, which in a pure complex would make U non-dense, contradicting the proviso). Complexes that are not locally finite (weak topology) are not stated. Accept the reading?

RamcovGX.tex:1548: 'a direct consequence of Propositions prop:Galoisian_semilocal and prop:universality' silently drops second countability, which prop:Galoisian_semilocal assumes. The theorem holds without it: (ii) ⇒ (i) of prop:Galoisian_semilocal does not use countability (discrete fibres + dense orbits give transitivity, GX.maxBranched_isGaloisian). The second and third assertions need an argument the paper does not give: H is the automorphism group of the universal map Φ : Ỹ^S → X, which acts transitively on the Φ-fibres because they are discrete (subsets of the discrete fibres of Ỹ^S) and its orbits are dense (Φ is quasi-Galoisian through the ordinary part); normality ⇔ X Galoisian uses the uniqueness of maps over Y agreeing at one ordinary point (GX.eq_of_comp_eq_of_mem_portly). The normality equivalence is proved for every H with H\\Ỹ^S ≃ X over Y.

kb_proposals: The fibre of a complete spread over a first countable base is completely metrizable (GX.isCompletelyMetrizableSpace_fiber, closed in a countable product of discrete DiscreteSets): Baire replaces inverse-limit cardinality arguments (countable fibre ⇒ isolated point).
Lifting a loop based at a singular point: cut it at an interior point (GX.tailHalf / GX.headHalfRev, whose symm.trans is the loop on the nose) and lift both halves from the ordinary midpoint.

Two maps over Y between branched coverings agreeing at one point over a portly O ⊆ ord(Y) are equal (GX.eq_of_comp_eq_of_mem_portly): the uniqueness lemma behind deck-group injectivity and normality arguments.
Pitfall: `open CategoryTheory` makes `Injective` ambiguous (CategoryTheory.Injective vs Function.Injective); write `CategoryTheory.Iso S S` instead of opening the namespace.

Identifiers starting with λ (λ', γλ) do not parse; and a structure field proof inside `toFun t := δ ⟨_, by …⟩` gave 'unknown free variable' in source'/target' — factor the reparametrisation into a named function I → I.

Radial criterion for slsc (GX.isSLSCAt_of_radial_contraction): for M ⊆ E normed, work in the subtype metric space ↥M; build the contraction homotopy as a subtype-valued ContinuousMap and Path.Homotopy by hand (Subtype.ext + simp for the boundary fields). Barycentric 'face absorbs the segment ]x,v]' is AffineIndependent.eq_of_sum_eq_sum_subtype on the two weight systems.
